translation:
The Zhizhen Yaolun (至真要大論) says: "Acrid and sweet disperse and effuse and are yang; sour and bitter surge and drain and are yin; the salty flavor surges and drains and is yin; the insipid flavor seeps and drains and is yang." Of these six, some disperse, some astringe, some relax, some bind urgently, some dry, some moisten, some harden, some lighten; one acts according to what is beneficial, thereby regulating its qi.

The Bencao (本草) says: "Medicinals have three grades. The upper grade is the sovereign (君), chiefly nourishing life, with slight toxicity, to correspond to heaven; the middle grade is the minister (臣), chiefly nourishing nature, with ordinary toxicity, to correspond to man; the lower grade is the assistant and courier (佐使), chiefly treating disease, with great toxicity, to correspond to earth."
translator_notes: 君臣佐使 rendered as sovereign/minister/assistant/courier with characters.
